description:
FOUND s506f (Opus, 2026-10-04): with #1702 the -n/-a/-F loops of t/run/switch{n,a,F}.t now RUN, and read
nothing, because each file does `BEGIN { ...; *ARGV = *DATA; }` and reads the loop's `<>`.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 618db500 and s506f):
  printf 'BEGIN { *ARGV = *DATA; }\nprint "[", scalar(<>), "]\\n";\n__DATA__\nd1\nd2\n' > ad.pl
  perl ad.pl </dev/null   -> [d1\n]
  pcl  ad.pl </dev/null   -> []          (also with <ARGV>)
  The same assignment at RUN time works (`*ARGV = *DATA; while (<>) {...}` -> both lines).

CAUSE (suspected, measure first): at BEGIN time DATA is not open yet (perl opens it when the parser
reaches __DATA__, but the GLOB alias makes ARGV and DATA one glob, so the later open is seen through
ARGV).  PCL's glob assignment copies the handle VALUE at assignment time.  Discriminating probe:
`BEGIN { *X = *DATA } print scalar(<X>)` -- if that fails too, it is the glob-value copy, not <>.

ROWS: run/switchn.t (2 rows: the loop reads nothing), run/switcha.t (2), run/switchF.t (2),
run/noswitch.t row 2.  Since s506f these files' rows are SHORTFALL (never produced), where before the
body ran once outside any loop and produced one failing row.
subject: `*ARGV = *DATA` in a BEGIN block does not alias: `<>` later reads nothing (at run time the same assignment works) -- t/run/switchn.t, switcha.t, switchF.t, noswitch.t
